title: Model tier is configuration
description:
A definition names a tier, not a model: `editorial` (writing and rewriting that readers see), `work` (structured tasks and checks), `bulk` (rating and bookkeeping), `decision` (the trained decision model). The site policy maps each tier to a model id, with the engine's defaults; the price table stays data. Changing a model is a policy change with a version, and each run records the model it used.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Changing a tier's model changes the next run with no deploy.
- Each run records its tier and model.
- A model missing from the price table is named, not treated as free.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- model-tiers.feature: an agent uses the model its tier maps to; a policy change switches it; the run records both; an unknown model id is refused when saved.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Spend, budgets and model tiers. Slice code G4 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
